note: Independent reading. The two starter books are what Sheila has actually read; suggestions are well-known middle-grade titles chosen for the reading skills the ISEE tests.

suggestions.title: The Secret Garden
suggestions.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
suggestions.why: Older, formal language and long descriptive passages — closest thing to an ISEE reading passage.

suggestions.title: Anne of Green Gables
suggestions.author: L. M. Montgomery
suggestions.why: Rich figurative language and a big vocabulary; a natural next step if she likes Little Women.

suggestions.title: The Westing Game
suggestions.author: Ellen Raskin
suggestions.why: A puzzle mystery — nothing is stated outright, so it is pure inference practice.

suggestions.title: Holes
suggestions.author: Louis Sachar
suggestions.why: Three timelines braided together; good for questions about how a text is organised.

suggestions.title: Number the Stars
suggestions.author: Lois Lowry
suggestions.why: Historical fiction: context clues and tone carry most of the meaning.

suggestions.title: Because of Winn-Dixie
suggestions.author: Kate DiCamillo
suggestions.why: Short chapters, and almost every feeling is implied rather than stated.

suggestions.title: Where the Mountain Meets the Moon
suggestions.author: Grace Lin
suggestions.why: Folktales nested inside a story — main idea and theme practice.

suggestions.title: A Wrinkle in Time
suggestions.author: Madeleine L'Engle
suggestions.why: Abstract ideas and harder vocabulary; a real step up.

suggestions.title: Wonder
suggestions.author: R. J. Palacio
suggestions.why: Several narrators tell the same events — point of view practice.

suggestions.title: The Wild Robot
suggestions.author: Peter Brown
suggestions.why: Plain sentences and strong cause and effect; an easy, enjoyable one between harder books.
